clue.text: In charge of manifest, briefly

blocks.note: overt means plainly visible, manifest

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of a ship's manifest, summed up in a few words.
explanation.walkthrough: OVERT loses its last letter to leave OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To be over a team or department is to have authority above it, so the preposition matches.

clue.text: Swear there's nothing in car

blocks.note: zero, shaped like the letter O
VW is Volkswagen, a car maker, standing for one of its cars

explanation.surface: Someone cursing because the car turns out to be empty.
explanation.definitionFit: To vow is to promise solemnly, the oath-taking sense of swear rather than cursing.

clue.text: He stepped down as 25 turned up - ciao!

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning a word up makes it read from the bottom, backwards

blocks.note: the answer to 25 down, a teacher
ciao is the Italian greeting, like hi

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster arrives with a breezy Italian hello as someone resigns.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, turning a word up reverses it. Rishi Sunak stood down as Conservative leader after the 2024 election defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rishi Sunak resigned as UK Prime Minister and party leader in 2024, a specific example of a man who stepped down.

clue.text: Time to question staff about flipping tough boss

indicators.note: something flipped is turned over, so the word reads the other way round

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to question is to ask
a mast is a tall pole or staff
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Time to grill employees about a boss who is tough to the point of exasperation.
explanation.walkthrough: T + ASK + MAST + ER, where ER is RE flipped. 'Flipping' passes for a mild British swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: A taskmaster is a demanding supervisor who drives people hard, exactly a tough boss.

clue.text: Take a chance, or rather don't when clothes shopping

blocks.note: first meaning: to chance your luck, to see what you can get away with
second meaning: read don't as don 't, put it on, as a shopper does in the fitting room

explanation.surface: Advice to gamble, then a reversal telling you not to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't' seems to forbid, but split as don 't it means put it on, the way a garment is tested in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for attempting a cheeky ploy, and literally for wearing a garment to test the fit.

clue.text: Ollie's partner almost finished composing rude song "stay firm"

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
composing music means arranging notes into a new order

blocks.note: Stan Laurel was Oliver Hardy's comedy partner
done means finished
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Laurel, nearly done writing a bawdy number, called it Stay Firm.
explanation.walkthrough: STAN + DON(E) + ESGROUND. Laurel and Hardy were the classic comedy double act, Stan and Ollie.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand your ground is an idiom for refusing to retreat or yield, which is staying firm.

clue.text: Autobiographical book from Bard in English and French: Raconteurs en vacance?

definitions.note: the answer is plural in form, but names a single book

blocks.note: the setter Bard refers to himself; in English that is me
the same pronoun in French
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A setter's life story told in two languages by holidaying storytellers.
explanation.walkthrough: ME + MOI + RS. The setter's own pseudonym stands for 'me', a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoirs are a written account of the author's own life, an autobiography.

clue.text: Miserable soul broken by clergyman - that hurts frightfully at first

blocks.note: taken as written
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title
the cry of pain
first letter

explanation.surface: A sad soul crushed by a priest, crying out at the frightening pain.
explanation.walkthrough: SO(RR + OW + F)UL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrowful means full of grief, a straightforward synonym for miserable.

clue.text: Speller considered 'nefarious' - "N … repeat the word? Right … ends with S"

blocks.note: the letter N spelled out as its name
to chant is to repeat words rhythmically
R is the abbreviation for right
the letter S spelled out as its name

explanation.surface: A spelling bee where a word is spelt out letter by letter, with requests to hear it again.
explanation.walkthrough: EN + CHANT + R + ESS. Spelling the letters out as names fits a speller, here a caster of spells.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchantress is a witch who casts spells, a 'speller', and such a figure is usually thought wicked.

clue.text: 'Banks of tomorrow' impress Treasury? Not true

blocks.note: first and last letters
first and last letters
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A question whether future banks will win over the Treasury, answered in the negative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks of' governs all three words that follow, not just tomorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Twisty describes something crooked or devious, so not straight or true.

clue.text: High-speed hand-walking contest is a very dangerous competition

blocks.note: first meaning, whimsical: a race run on the arms instead of legs
second meaning: nations competing to build up weapons

explanation.surface: A daft gymnastic sprint on the hands is said to be perilous.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase literally, a race on one's arms; the second is its real meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: An arms race is rivalry between states to stockpile weapons, a contest that risks war.

clue.text: Dependent on drugs, did cadet collapse?

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Being addicted means being physically or mentally hooked on a substance.

clue.text: Dwindling workplace doing this to make something cool

blocks.note: first meaning: declining, falling away

blocks.note: second meaning, cryptic: OFFICE losing its OFF leaves ICE

explanation.surface: An office in decline, and someone trying to make it trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half describes what the answer does: an office that drops its first three letters becomes ice, which is cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures that are dropping off are decreasing, so the phrase means dwindling.

clue.text: This shows pressure is zero impediment

blocks.note: taken as written
zero, shaped like the letter O
a bar is an obstacle or impediment

explanation.surface: A claim that some gauge of stress reveals a total lack of obstacles.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: There are three in there, four in that one and six in my pocket

definitions.text: There are three in there, four in that one and six in my pocket

blocks.note: surface reading: counting objects in containers
setter's reading: count the letters of a certain kind in the words there, that one and my pocket

explanation.surface: Someone tallying coins or sweets in various places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' has T, H, R; 'that one' has T, H, T, N; 'my pocket' has M, Y, P, C, K, T, counting Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue counts letters that are not vowels in the quoted words, so the things counted are this letter class.

clue.text: Soft rock from 5?

explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: 5 down, STAND ONE'S GROUND, is read as 'ground STAND ONES', the instruction that turns this answer into those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandstone is a sedimentary stone of compressed grains, fairly easily worn away, so a soft rock.

clue.text: Fellow worried about cheese

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
as in 'what's eating you?': ate means troubled

explanation.surface: A man anxious about some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: F + ETA, which is ATE turned about.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a crumbly white Greek cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Fourth in Nicolas Cage's golf tournament

blocks.note: fourth letter
a pen is an enclosure for animals, a cage

explanation.surface: The actor Nicolas Cage finishing fourth at a golf event.
explanation.walkthrough: The actor's name splits apart: Nicolas supplies one letter and Cage becomes a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The Open is the British golf championship, one of the four majors, often just called the Open.

clue.text: Old footballer's right to devour fashion mag and Bridget Jones's Diary?

explanation.definitionFit: Helen Fielding's comic novel sold millions of copies, so it is an example of a hit book, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Forbid one to leave peaceful meal

last letter of Henry

clue.text: Co-operation in Parkrun is one-sided
